title: Smallness of extensions of two essentially small object classes
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal T$ be a pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] whose Hom sets are $\mathcal V$-small. Let $\mathcal P,\mathcal Q$ be classes of objects of $\mathcal T$, each admitting a $\mathcal V$-small family of representatives up to isomorphism. Define $\mathcal P*\mathcal Q$ to consist of the objects isomorphic to a middle term $M$ in a distinguished triangle $B\to M\to C\xrightarrow{\delta}B[1]$ with $B\in\mathcal P$ and $C\in\mathcal Q$. Then $\mathcal P*\mathcal Q$ admits a $\mathcal V$-small family of representatives up to isomorphism. This assertion does not require functorial cone choices, abelian hearts, boundedness, or Tor amplitude.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: each truncation extension is classified by an ambient Hom set; Stacks derived.tex Tags 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle) and 014B (lemma-cone-triangle-unique-isomorphism).

proof.text: Choose representative families $(B_i)_{i\in I}$ for $\mathcal P$ and $(C_j)_{j\in J}$ for $\mathcal Q$, with $I,J$ $\mathcal V$-small and $B_i\in\mathcal P$, $C_j\in\mathcal Q$. Representatives may repeat. For each $(i,j)$ the set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(C_j,B_i[1])$ is $\mathcal V$-small by the local-smallness hypothesis. Thus the dependent sum $S=\coprod_{(i,j)\in I\times J}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(C_j,B_i[1])$ is $\mathcal V$-small: a small union of small sets belongs to the fixed Grothendieck universe. If either class is empty, its representative family and $S$ are empty and the extension class is empty as well.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: extensions classified by ambient Hom sets; explicit fixed-universe counting

proof.text: For $s=(i,j,\delta)\in S$, apply TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] to $\delta:C_j\to B_i[1]$. Twice inverse-rotate its distinguished completion using TR2, and identify $(B_i[1])[-1]$ with $B_i$ using the inverse shift. This gives a distinguished triangle $B_i\to M_s\to C_j\xrightarrow{\delta}B_i[1]$. The two inverse rotations retain $\delta$ as the third arrow, with the rotation signs in the other arrows. Choose one such triangle for each $s$; its middle term belongs to $\mathcal P*\mathcal Q$. This is a choice indexed by $S$ and imposes no naturality requirement.

source.place: Tag 0145 (definition-triangulated-category), TR1 and TR2; Tag 014B (lemma-cone-triangle-unique-isomorphism), existence by TR1, applied after rotation

proof.text: Given a distinguished triangle $B\to M\to C\xrightarrow{\gamma}B[1]$ with $B\in\mathcal P$, $C\in\mathcal Q$, choose $i,j$ and isomorphisms $a:B\xrightarrow{\sim}B_i$, $c:C\xrightarrow{\sim}C_j$. Set $\delta=a[1]\circ\gamma\circ c^{-1}$ and $s=(i,j,\delta)$. Then $a[1]\circ\gamma=\delta\circ c$. Twice rotate this triangle and the triangle chosen for $s$. Their first arrows are $\gamma:C\to B[1]$ and $\delta:C_j\to B_i[1]$, so this equality is exactly the square required by TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. TR3 supplies a morphism between these distinguished triangles whose first two components are $c$ and $a[1]$ and whose third component is some $d:M[1]\to M_s[1]$.

source.place: Tag 0145 (definition-triangulated-category), TR2 and TR3; Tag 014B (lemma-cone-triangle-unique-isomorphism), comparison by TR3

proof.text: In the morphism of twice-rotated distinguished triangles just constructed, $c$ and $a[1]$ are isomorphisms. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], $d$ is an isomorphism. Applying the inverse shift from [def-weil-triangulated-category] gives $M\cong M_s$. Every object of $\mathcal P*\mathcal Q$ is isomorphic to such an $M$ by its defining condition, hence to some $M_s$ by composition of isomorphisms. Conversely each $M_s$ belongs to that class by step 2. Therefore the family $(M_s)_{s\in S}$ is the required $\mathcal V$-small family of representatives.

source.place: Tag 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle), applied to the twice-rotated triangles; Tag 014B (lemma-cone-triangle-unique-isomorphism)
